scope: Second single fastboot boot of the same entry-probe-06 package, to test whether the post-arm_init behaviour varies between boots
conclusion: The second boot of the same package reproduced the first one band for band: the user read the photograph and confirmed the band set is the same, only the camera angle differs. So the post-arm_init behaviour is REPRODUCIBLE, and the earlier claim that it varies between boots was wrong - that comparison was across packages (v11 showed purple and a panic, v13 does not), not across boots of one package. The frontier is stable: arm_vm_init reached, executed to +0x54, no panic hook, no panic text, no exception report.
hypothesis_for_the_package_difference: v13 added thirteen more function-entry hooks, among them SecureDTLookupEntry, early_random and pe_arm_get_soc_base_phys, which are called repeatedly. Each call now redraws a 32-row band, which is about 23000 store instructions, so the instrumentation itself may have slowed the kernel enough to change its behaviour, or held it in a long critical section. A draw-once guard per hook is the obvious fix and is not yet implemented or tested.
not_proven: the cause of the v11/v13 difference
whether the stop is a hang, a watchdog reset or a fault
the colours of the two lower bands, which the photo places at 656 and 848 by position
